title: Corn flour, masa harina, white or yellow, dry, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Corn flour (masa harina) is a dry, finely ground product made from whole corn kernels, widely used in Latin American cuisine. Both white and yellow varieties have a mild sweet corn flavor, with the yellow version containing carotenoids that give it a bright hue. The flour is sold dry and ready to use without any pre‑treatment.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Masa harina is the base for traditional Mexican foods such as tortillas, tamales and enchiladas.
Yellow corn flour contains carotenoids, which increase its provitamin A content.
White corn flour is often chosen when a neutral color and flavor are desired.
Corn flour is naturally gluten‑free, making it suitable for gluten‑free diets.
Traditionally the flour is mixed with water (forming a “nixtamal”) before cooking, which improves texture.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides a steady source of energy due to its complex carbohydrate content.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Both soluble and insoluble fibers support healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with wheat flour, corn flour has a lower fat content, which can be advantageous in low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides thiamine, niacin and folate, important for metabolic processes.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Corn flour can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking or fermenting the dough can lower its level.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Corn flour is used to make tortilla dough, tamale masa, corn flatbreads, as a coating for frying, and as a thickener for soups and sauces. Mix the dry flour with water (about 1 part flour to 2 parts water) until smooth, let it rest 15‑30 minutes, then shape and cook.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store corn flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth and fat oxidation.
